title: Roald Dahl: Crash and Chocolate
dek: The pilot who survived the desert and gave children dangerous stories.
mortality_event: 1940 RAF crash in the Libyan desert causing skull fracture, facial injuries, and temporary blindness.

sources.name: RAF Benevolent Fund: Roald Dahl’s RAF career

citation_passage: Roald Dahl was a British writer whose career included wartime service as a Royal Air Force pilot. In September 1940, unable to find his destination airstrip, he crash-landed in the North African desert and escaped his burning aircraft. After hospital treatment and rehabilitation, he returned to flying. His account of the ordeal later reached the Saturday Evening Post, and he went on to write children's stories including Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. This seven-page biographical comic considers danger, recovery, and storytelling. The RAF Benevolent Fund describes his military career; the official biography also acknowledges the harm of his antisemitic remarks.
